question: Which of the following is NOT a property of similar triangles?

options.text: Ratio of areas of two similar triangles = Ratio of squares of corresponding segments obtained by corresponding angle bisectors.
Ratio of areas of two similar triangles = Ratio of squares of corresponding medians
Ratio of areas of two Similar triangles = Ratio of squares of corresponding altitudes
Ratio of areas of two similar triangles= Ratio of corresponding segments obtained by corresponding angle bisectors.

solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The ratio of the areas of two similar triangles is always equal to the square of the ratio of their corresponding linear dimensions.

Linear dimensions include side lengths, altitudes, medians, perimeters, and angle bisectors.

Options 1, 2, and 3 correctly state that the area ratio equals the ratio of the squares of these corresponding lengths.

Option 4 incorrectly equates the area ratio directly to the linear segment ratio without squaring it, making it dimensionally incorrect.

**∴ The correct answer is Ratio of areas of two similar triangles = Ratio of corresponding segments obtained by corresponding angle bisectors.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

⇒ Let there be two similar triangles, ΔABC ∼ ΔPQR.

**Concept Used:**

⇒ When two triangles are similar, the ratio of their areas is strictly equal to the square of the ratio of their corresponding side lengths.

⇒ Area(ΔABC) ÷ Area(ΔPQR) = (AB ÷ PQ)² = (BC ÷ QR)² = (AC ÷ PR)²

⇒ This fundamental similarity property also holds true for any other corresponding 1-dimensional segments like altitudes, medians, and angle bisectors.

**Calculations:**

⇒ Checking Option 1: Ratio of areas = (Ratio of angle bisectors)². This is a true geometric property.

⇒ Checking Option 2: Ratio of areas = (Ratio of medians)². This is a true geometric property.

⇒ Checking Option 3: Ratio of areas = (Ratio of altitudes)². This is a true geometric property.

⇒ Checking Option 4: Ratio of areas = Ratio of angle bisectors. This is mathematically false because Area is a 2-dimensional quantity, meaning its comparative ratio must always be derived from the square of any given 1-dimensional length ratio.

**∴ The correct answer is Ratio of areas of two similar triangles = Ratio of corresponding segments obtained by corresponding angle bisectors.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Ratio of Perimeters in Similar Triangles

The ratio of the perimeters of two similar triangles is equal to the direct ratio of their corresponding sides (without any squaring). Perimeter represents a linear 1D measurement.

Angle Bisector Theorem

An interior angle bisector of a triangle divides the opposite side into two proportional segments that correspond to the lengths of the other two adjacent sides: BD ÷ DC = AB ÷ AC.

Similarity Criteria

Two triangles are determined to be completely similar if they satisfy the AAA (Angle-Angle-Angle), SAS (Side-Angle-Side), or SSS (Side-Side-Side) criteria. Similar triangles always maintain identical shapes but may differ in size.
